title: Cheese Quesadilla
subtitle: Melted cheese in a crispy toasted flour tortilla
excerpt: A flour tortilla folded over a generous layer of cheese and toasted in a dry pan until the outside is crisp and golden and the inside is completely melted. Ready in under 5 minutes.
sourceNotes: Cheese quesadillas: one of the simplest Tex-Mex dishes, a direct descendant of the Mexican quesadilla made from corn or flour tortillas with Oaxacan string cheese. The Tex-Mex version uses flour tortillas and cheddar. Based on classic American and Mexican home-cooking tradition.

glossaryTerms.definition: A Mexican and Tex-Mex dish consisting of a tortilla filled with cheese, folded or sandwiched, and toasted until the cheese melts and the tortilla crisps. The name comes from the Spanish word 'queso', meaning cheese.

content.text: is a flour tortilla toasted in a dry pan with cheese melted inside. The cheese provides both filling and the glue that holds the folded tortilla shut. Two things make the difference: grating the cheese finely so it melts quickly, and not moving the quesadilla until the underside is properly golden.
A frying pan wide enough to hold the whole tortilla without folding makes this easier. A 30 cm pan fits a standard medium tortilla with room to handle it.
Heat a dry frying pan over medium heat. Lay one flour tortilla flat in the pan.
Scatter {{cheddar}} of grated cheese over half the tortilla, leaving a 1 cm border. Fold the empty half over the cheese to make a semicircle.
Cook for 1.5-2 minutes without moving until the underside is golden and crisp. Flip and cook the other side for 1-1.5 minutes. Rest on a board for 1 minute before cutting into wedges.
Serve with soured cream and sliced jalapeño if using.

items.symptom: Cheese isn't melted when the tortilla is golden
items.cause: Heat too high, or cheese not grated finely enough
items.fix: Medium heat is the right level. Finely grated cheese melts faster than roughly torn pieces. Don't rush the heat.

items.cause: Cheese hasn't melted enough to act as glue
items.fix: Wait until the underside is golden before flipping. A quick press with a spatula after flipping helps the two sides stay together.

items.symptom: Inside is soggy rather than melted
items.cause: Pan too cool; the tortilla steamed instead of toasting
items.fix: The pan must be hot before the tortilla goes in. A dry pan, medium heat, no oil.

items.symptom: Cheese leaks out and burns on the pan
items.cause: Cheese placed too close to the fold edge
items.fix: Leave a 1 cm border along the folded edge so the cheese doesn't escape when the tortilla is pressed shut.

content.text: The cheese quesadilla is the simplest Tex-Mex dish: one pan, two ingredients, and five minutes. In Mexico, quesadillas are made with corn tortillas and Oaxacan string cheese. The Tex-Mex version uses flour tortillas and cheddar. This is the format that spread into American homes and then into British ones. It doesn't announce itself, but it ends up being made every week.
